comments.body:
Premise validated on base ae6f2ac57a: ruff C901 census over src/rebar/graph reproduced the ticket's four hotspots EXACTLY — _find_direct_blockers 18, _get_all_blocked_by 20, check_cycle_at_level 16, detect_newly_unblocked 22. No sibling landing had moved or already-reduced them, so the plan stood as written.

Plan-review: the inherited PASS attestation was foreign_key (signed by principal ade0f2ef, this env is b8a354e0), so review-plan was re-run here. First pass BLOCKed on G1G2: the plan named 'tests/unit + tests/interfaces' as the behavioral oracle, but neither contains any of these symbols — the real oracle is tests/scripts/graph/ plus tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py. Corrected that, and also applied the two apply-now advisories: (G6) specified the bfs contract as an ACCUMULATOR-returning walk rather than a visited-returning one, because _get_all_blocked_by returns 'blocked' — which excludes the seed and includes targets with no backing dir — so a visited-returning bfs would have silently changed check_would_create_cycle's membership test; (E6) added a characterization test for exactly that property, since no existing test pinned it. Second pass PASS + signed, only a deferred P6 (compound ACs). Claimed cleanly.

Implementation landed as planned, behavior-preserving:
- _loader.load_indexed_states — the reduce_all -> drop error/fsck -> index loop, previously duplicated verbatim in _find_direct_blockers and _compute_dep_graph, now defined once (reached via the reducer module attribute so the existing patch point still works).
- _relations.bfs(starts, neighbors_fn) — accumulator BFS skeleton; visited is passed to neighbors_fn read-only because both callers consult it when deciding what to yield.
- _blockers: split into _own_depends_on_blockers / _blocks_targeting (the two sources its own docstring already named), dedup preserved across the two.
- _graph: _reduce_or_none / _blocks_targets / _dependents_of / _is_at_level / _same_level_neighbors extracted; check_cycle_at_level's mid-loop early return became 'source_id in bfs(...)' (equivalent: the seed cannot be source_id since the self-loop case returns first).
- _unblock: _read_tombstone_status / _load_states_with_tombstones / _is_closed_after_batch / _was_already_unblocked / _select_newly_unblocked. Kept separate from load_indexed_states — tombstone semantics differ.
- _ready.py, _status.py::_get_ticket_status and _unblock.py::batch_close_operations untouched, as scoped.

Result: all four functions now measure CCN <= 7 (targets were <=8/<=8/<=8/<=12), so --update-stale REMOVED all four baseline entries rather than lowering them — they no longer exceed the 15 threshold at all. check_complexity_baseline.py --check: active=55 new=0 increased=0 stale=0.

Gates: 118/118 in tests/scripts/graph/ + tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py green with zero edits to existing tests; the new characterization test was verified passing on the PRE-refactor base first (it characterizes current behavior) and still passes after. make lint green, make typecheck green (518 files), all argument-less check_* gates exit 0, all four generators produce no diff. Full CI suite running now.

Pushed as Gerrit change 1708 (commit 6c62cfb9ff, https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1708).

Full local gate set green before push: make lint, make typecheck (518 files), all argument-less check_* gates exit 0, check_complexity_baseline.py --check = active=55 new=0 increased=0 stale=0, all four generators no-diff, and the CI-parity suite (pytest -m 'not integration and not external' -n 3 --dist worksteal --timeout=300) = 12622 passed, 52 skipped, exit 0.

Note on the baseline diff: it is a pure 4-line DELETION, not a lowering. All four functions fell below the C901 threshold of 15 entirely (measured <= 7), so --update-stale drained their entries. Per .github/complexity-baseline.README.md, removing an entry is an allowed shrink-only change, so the lock gate should accept it. Sibling b2bb (compact split) also regenerates this file; if it lands first the rebase will need a re-run of --update-stale, which is the epic's expected landing-order behavior, not a defect.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Gerrit LLM-Review +1 (PASS) on change 1708 with 3 advisory findings, all marked resolved and non-blocking. Recording them here rather than amending, since amending would reset the +1, re-run CI, and widen the window for a baseline-file rebase against sibling b2bb for no behavioral gain:

1. (maintainability, _blockers.py) The guard 'relation not in _BLOCKING_RELATIONS or relation != "depends_on"' is redundant — depends_on is a member of the frozenset, so the first clause is dead. Accurate. It is a faithful carry-over of the original's nested 'if relation in _BLOCKING_RELATIONS: if relation == "depends_on"', preserved deliberately in a behavior-preserving refactor and explained in the new docstring. Removing it would also strand _status.py's _BLOCKING_RELATIONS re-export, which exists solely for _blockers and which this ticket scopes as untouched; other users (_hierarchy, doctor) import the constant straight from _relations, so the tidy fix is to retire that indirection in its own change.

2. (tests, _graph.py) check_cycle_at_level's target-side level guard (_is_at_level refusing to traverse into a neighbour of a different ticket_type) is untested — every existing test uses one uniform level. True, and PRE-EXISTING: the same guard was inline in the original loop and equally uncovered. The extraction did not change it.

3. (tests, _unblock.py) _load_states_with_tombstones (stub-yielding when reduce returns None but a tombstone exists, tombstone-status override, malformed-tombstone -> 'deleted') has no test driving it through detect_newly_unblocked. Also pre-existing: that logic was inline in detect_newly_unblocked before this change with the same coverage.

Findings 2 and 3 are genuine coverage gaps in the graph subsystem that this refactor surfaced by naming the seams, but did not introduce. They are worth a follow-up ticket under the ae1b remediation epic rather than scope creep here.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Four `graph` functions carry moderate cyclomatic complexity in the checked-in ratchet (`.github/complexity-baseline.json`), re-measured on this base and unchanged: `_blockers.py::_find_direct_blockers` (18), `_graph.py::_get_all_blocked_by` (20), `_graph.py::check_cycle_at_level` (16), `_unblock.py::detect_newly_unblocked` (22). LOW-RISK: pure logic, `graph.*` is in the mypy strictness ratchet, extensive existing tests, zero in-progress contention. The high-risk orchestrators `next_batch.compute` (CCN 42) and `import_ndjson.import_tickets` (CCN 45) are deliberately EXCLUDED. Flagged by audit ae1b.

## Root cause (architectural)
`graph/_loader.py` is a 15-line shim that stops at raw `reduce_ticket`/`reduce_all_tickets`, so higher-level query logic is hand-rolled per call-site. TWO distinct patterns recur and drive the CCN:
1. The **exact** "reduce_all → drop `error`/`fsck_needed` → index by id" loop is duplicated verbatim in `_find_direct_blockers` (`_blockers.py:33-40`) and `_compute_dep_graph` (`_graph.py:65-72`) — identical policy (`reduce_all_tickets(exclude_archived=False, exclude_session_logs=True)` + drop error/fsck).
2. `_get_all_blocked_by` (`_graph.py:127`) and `check_cycle_at_level` (`_graph.py:223`) each re-implement an FS-walking BFS skeleton (queue/visited + per-node `reduce_ticket` + try/except + dep-scan).

## Approach (conservative, behavior-preserving — reconcile divergent node-sets, do NOT unify them)
Add exactly two shared helpers and refactor onto them WITHOUT changing any function's node-set or traversal results:

1. `graph/_loader.py`: add `load_indexed_states(tracker_dir) -> dict[str, dict]` reproducing pattern (1) EXACTLY (`reduce_all_tickets(exclude_archived=False, exclude_session_logs=True)` via the `reducer` module attribute so the existing `_loader_module.reducer.reduce_all_tickets` patch point still works, then drop `error`/`fsck_needed`, index by `ticket_id`). Apply it at ONLY the two identical-policy sites: `_blockers.py:33-40` and `_graph.py:65-72`.

2. `graph/_relations.py` (already hosts `build_blocked_by`): add a shared **accumulator** BFS skeleton, `bfs(starts, neighbors_fn) -> set[str]`, where `neighbors_fn(node, visited) -> Iterable[str]`. **Contract (stated explicitly because the two call-sites' outputs differ structurally):**
   - `bfs` owns ONLY queue/visited bookkeeping: pop, skip if visited, mark visited, call `neighbors_fn`, add every yielded id to an **accumulator** set and enqueue it when not already visited. All I/O, reduce calls, exception-swallowing and filtering stay in each `neighbors_fn`; `bfs` has no policy.
   - The returned set is the **accumulator**, NOT `visited`: a start node is absent unless a real edge yields it, and a yielded id is present even when no ticket dir backs it (never dequeued). That is exactly `_get_all_blocked_by`'s `blocked` set (`_graph.py:151` adds every `blocks` target before any existence check). A `visited`-returning bfs would wrongly include the seed and break `check_would_create_cycle`'s `target_id in _get_all_blocked_by(source_id)` test.
   - `visited` is passed to `neighbors_fn` (read-only) because both loops consult it when deciding what to yield (`_graph.py:160-161`, `:266`); without it the accumulator would differ.
   - `_get_all_blocked_by` becomes `return bfs([ticket_id], neighbors)`, `neighbors` reproducing its per-node behavior verbatim (dir-exists → `reduce_ticket` → yield `blocks` targets unconditionally; then `os.listdir` → skip visited/hidden/non-dirs → `reduce_ticket` → yield entries whose `depends_on` targets `current`).
   - `check_cycle_at_level` becomes `return source_id in bfs([target_id], neighbors)` after its existing `not level` / self-loop early returns. Its mid-loop `if current == source_id: return True` is equivalent: the seed cannot be `source_id` (self-loop already returned), so `source_id` is dequeued iff some `neighbors_fn` yielded it, iff it is in the accumulator. Dropping the early return changes only how far the walk goes, never the boolean; the walk is bounded by the level-filtered dep component reachable from `target_id`, not by tracker size, and no perf test covers this function.
   - Both keep raw `reduce_ticket` (NO error/fsck filter, NO session-log exclusion) — NOT routed through `load_indexed_states`, so their node-set is unchanged.

3. `_find_direct_blockers`: use `load_indexed_states` for the load branch; extract the two blocking sources named in its own docstring into `_own_depends_on_blockers` / `_blocks_targeting` helpers to cut branching.

4. `detect_newly_unblocked`: extract its inline scandir+tombstone loader (`_unblock.py:53-80`) into a named module-level helper `_load_states_with_tombstones` (kept in `_unblock.py`; NOT merged with `load_indexed_states` — its tombstone semantics differ); keep the readiness logic and the existing `build_blocked_by` reuse.

OUT OF SCOPE (divergent semantics): `_ready.py` (dependency-light — must NOT import the heavy `_loader`), `_status.py::_get_ticket_status` (a status *predicate* mapping error→closed, not a loader), `_unblock.py::batch_close_operations`.

Rationale (G6): centralizing only the provably-identical loop (site 1) plus one accumulator-BFS skeleton lowers CCN and removes the growth-driving duplication, while leaving each function's node-set/traversal identical — so the change is behavior-preserving and the next graph query has a loader/bfs to reuse instead of hand-rolling a fifth copy.

## Scope
- `graph/_loader.py` add `load_indexed_states`; `graph/_relations.py` add accumulator `bfs`.
- `graph/_blockers.py`, `graph/_graph.py`, `graph/_unblock.py` — refactor the four functions onto those helpers as described above.
- `tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_cycles.py` — ADD one characterization test (below).
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` — regenerate (`python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --update-stale`), shrink-only.

## Verification (behavior-preserving refactor)
- **The behavioral oracle is the whole `tests/scripts/graph/` directory (notably `test_graph_cycles.py`, `test_graph_traversal.py`, `test_graph_unresolved_blocker.py`, `test_graph_perf.py`) plus `tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py`** — the suites that actually import the four functions. They pass UNCHANGED (no edits to existing tests).
- **One NEW characterization test** is required because no existing test pins the accumulator-vs-visited distinction: assert `_get_all_blocked_by` still returns a `blocks` target whose ticket dir does NOT exist (unconditional add), and that the seed id is absent from the result. Write it RED-first against `origin/main` (it must pass there, proving it characterizes current behavior) before the refactor.
- Complexity gate green with the four ceilings regenerated downward; `mypy src/rebar/graph` + `make lint` green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `.github/complexity-baseline.json` records `_find_direct_blockers` ≤ 8, `_get_all_blocked_by` ≤ 8, `check_cycle_at_level` ≤ 8, `detect_newly_unblocked` ≤ 12 (verified: `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exits 0).
- [x] The inline "reduce_all → drop error/fsck → index" loop is gone from `_find_direct_blockers` and `_compute_dep_graph`; both call `load_indexed_states` (verified by reading the two functions).
- [x] `_ready.py`, `_status.py::_get_ticket_status`, and `_unblock.py::batch_close_operations` are unchanged (verified: `git diff origin/main` touches none of those three symbols).
- [x] `_get_all_blocked_by` and `check_cycle_at_level` return results identical to origin/main (verified: `tests/scripts/graph/` and `tests/scripts/test_ticket_unblock.py` pass with no edits to existing tests).
- [x] The new characterization test asserts `_get_all_blocked_by` includes a `blocks` target with no backing ticket dir and excludes the seed id (verified: it passes on origin/main AND after the refactor).
- [x] `mypy src/rebar/graph` is green.
- [x] `make lint` is green.
